cells.tense: You are steady enough to give from what you have, and you decide where it goes.
cells.ask: Name one person and one thing you could hand them this week, then do that one thing and stop there.
cells.core:
You're not scrambling to keep up and you're not holding back for show. What you have is settled enough that you can pass some of it along, and you pick who gets it. Giving is a choice you make, not a leak. People around you can feel that in how it lands, because you're not spending tomorrow's resources today.

It keeps working as long as you keep deciding where it goes. One thing is yours to hand over, and the rest stays yours. That's a full hand opening on purpose and closing again. It lands because the person on the other side can tell it was picked for them, and the deciding stays yours the whole way through.
cells.sheetLine: You give from a full hand, and you decide where it goes.
cells.verb: Holding strength outward so resources move between people by measure
cells.place: At the point of choosing what this is for, and for whom

cells.tense: You are spending ahead on help the moment has not asked for yet.
cells.ask: Wait until someone actually asks, then give exactly what they asked for and nothing more.
cells.core:
You're already solving tomorrow's need before anyone has named it. People and plans get handed what you think they'll want, and you pay for it out of strength you haven't been given yet. It feels like readiness. A settled kind of support looks different — it knows how much it has, stops there, and the help lands at the moment it's wanted.

Push past that and the hand keeps moving after the moment has passed. The reserve you were trying to hand off is the first thing you lose, because you're spending next month's fuel on a road you haven't reached. What you have today is enough for today. Sit on the impulse to pre-solve, and the support stays support instead of supervision.
cells.sheetLine: You already gave next month's help before it was needed.

cells.tense: You stopped handing anything across, some time back, in a room that is already behind you.
cells.ask: Tell one person one thing you can actually give them this week — then let them decide whether to take it.
cells.core:
You have something to hand over and your hands aren't open. Direction hasn't stopped in you; the offering has. A door that's behind you still has a grip on the moment, which is why it feels risky to put anything outward. A full hand opening because it decided to looks like support landing without needing a particular answer back.

What's here now isn't the strength — it's being out of contact with anyone long enough to offer it. Pick one thing small enough that you can let it leave without knowing how it lands. That's the step. The strength is right behind it, still yours, waiting on a second hand to reach toward.
cells.sheetLine: You have something to hand over and you have stopped handing it.
cells.verb: Holding strength outward so resources move between people by measure

cells.tense: You are steadying what stands and moving what needs moving, and calling that nothing you decided.
cells.ask: Say out loud, once, that a direction you have already been holding is one you chose.
cells.core:
You keep the room steady. You set what moves, hold what stands, move what's needed — and you call it nothing. The directing is already happening, and no part of you has admitted it's yours. That's why it feels like something that arrives on its own instead of a choice you made. Done with the awareness that you picked it, the same acts get clearer.

A direction isn't something you hope for; it's the light you've already chosen and are steering by. And you are steering. The one who's been running this hasn't been credited, and that's the only thing out of step. Put your name on one direction you are already holding, and the support gets clear instead of automatic.
cells.sheetLine: You are already directing this. You just call it nothing you did.
